newsitem.title: USA: Key Bank-NY, Swiss Bank enliven US corp bond sector.
newsitem.headline: Key Bank-NY, Swiss Bank enliven US corp bond sector.

text.p: A few investment-grade corporate bond issues have appeared in the primary arena, breathing fresh air into a subdued primary market, dealers said.
"Overall a quiet holiday week is expected, however, two banks are in the market," said one syndicate source.
Swiss Bank Corp is expected to tap the market with a $400 million two-part AA2/AA rated subordinated notes via Swiss Bank. Both tranches are noncallable, sources said.

The deal consist of a 10-year maturity with price talk seen at 50 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The second maturity consist of a 30-year issue with price talk seen in the 70 basis points range, sources added.

In addition, Key Bank-NY is expected to price $165 million in A1/A-minus rated subordinated notes due 2008 via Salomon Brothers. Price talk on the issue is in the mid-70 basis points range, dealers said.

Amid the slow pre-holiday week and a recent backup in U.S. Treasury yields, the deals are expected to go well -- despite the subdued tone in the marketplace -- as both issues are higher rated credits, dealers said.
"Swiss bank is a AA-rated bank, they're going to get a tight spread anyway," said one syndicate source.
Another syndicate source added, "There is an outside possibility that both deals have been hedged in the marketplace and therefore decided to wreak the benefit of their hedge."
As the market heads into a holiday and desks continue thinly staffed, activity is expected to remain very light, dealers said.

The Public Securities Association has recommended an early 1400 EDT/1800 GMT close for the U.S. Treasury market on Friday, ahead of Monday's Labor Day holiday when U.S. financial markets will be closed.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is up 10/32 at 97-6/32 to yield 6.97 percent.
